MEMORANDUM

    Date:              October 2, 2026

    To:                Tahoe Transportation District (TTD) Board of Directors

    From:              TTD Staff – DeDe Aspero, Human Resources/Risk Manager

    Subject:           Review and Approval of the Selection of the Employee Health Benefit Program
                       for the Period December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027


    Action Requested:
    Staff requests the Board to review and approve the selection of the Employee Health Benefit
    Program for non-bargaining employees for the period December 1, 2026 through November 30,
    2027.

    Fiscal Impact:
    The management team has reviewed the proposals and recommends the Board approve the
    renewal medical plan (PPO Gold Plus) and a buy-up plan (PPO Gold Plus National) from
    Hometown Health. If these plans are selected, the Employee Health Benefit Program is
    expected to cost approximately $393,513 annually. There is a 7.8% increase in medical
    coverage, 1.9% increase for dental coverage, and 8.3% for short term disability. Vision and life
    insurance were presented with a rate guarantee from fiscal year 2026. The fiscal year 2027
    budget included an 18% increase over prior year for planning purposes, so the increases are
    well within budget. The program consists of:
         • Medical coverage           $356,760
         • Dental coverage              $26,640
         • Vision coverage               $4,390
         • Life insurance                $2,915
         • Short-term disability         $2,808

    As a small employer and having less than fifty employees in this group, the rates for the medical
    plan are based on age for everyone covered. The lower than budgeted rate increase allows
    TTD to maintain coverage for employees at 100%. For dependent coverage, employees pay
    55% of the age-based premium rate and TTD pays the remaining 45%.

    This year we are introducing an optional enhanced medical buy-up plan giving employees the
    choice for broader coverage. The buy-up plan allows medical treatment out of state through the
    Cigna network. Because this is optional, the full additional cost of the buy-up premium is paid by
    the employee through convenient pre-tax payroll deductions.

    Background:
    TTD supports two health care plans for its employees. The Employee Health Benefit Program is
    for the non-bargaining employees and provides medical, dental, vision, life insurance/accidental

death and dismemberment (AD&D), and short-term disability. An annual increase is estimated
and included in the budget, followed by an annual quote process as the end of the health
insurance term nears. The Employee Health Benefits Program is essential for recruiting and
retaining employees. An excellent benefits package that includes health coverage is extremely
important for employee retention, because it shows employees that their employer is invested in
their overall health and future. With increasing healthcare costs, ensuring that TTD employees
have access to high-quality and affordable care is a priority.

The second health care plan is for the represented employees and is provided through the
Teamsters Union and Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). Their plan includes medical,
dental, vision, and life insurance. The CBA stipulates the annual increase in cost to TTD for its
employee coverage, which is built into the annual budget. Their plan is on a calendar year and
coverage begins January 1.

Discussion:
The Human Resources/Risk Manager contacted LP Insurance to request group insurance
options for the upcoming plan year. LP Insurance presented the current carrier Hometown
Health and Aetna bid responses and was unable to secure quotes from United, Cigna, or
Anthem as they declined to quote. The request for market survey information was directed at
medical only and focused on coverage comparable to what is currently in place. The additional
fringe benefits that include dental, vision, life insurance/AD&D and short-term disability either
remained consistent with rates and coverage from the 2026 plan year or had a small increase.

Open enrollment will be held November 2 through 13, 2026, when the non-bargaining
employees can review current benefit coverage to ensure what they have in place continues to
meet their needs and the needs of their family members. New medical and vision coverage will
begin on December 1, 2026, with the dental, life insurance/AD&D, and short-term disability
benefit effective January 1, 2027.

Additional Information:
If you have any questions or comments regarding this item, please contact DeDe Aspero at
daspero@tahoetransportation.org or (775) 589-5326.

MEMORANDUM

Date:             October 2, 2026

To:               Tahoe Transportation District (TTD) Board of Directors

From:             Leslie Conard, TTD Finance Manager

Subject:          Approve an increase to the Executive Director’s signing authority from $75,000 to
                  $100,000 for contracts, agreements, purchase orders, and other authorized
                  expenditures, subject to applicable budget and procurement requirements.



Action Requested:
It is requested that the TTD Board of Directors approve an increase to the Executive Director’s signing
authority from $75,000 to $100,000 for contracts, agreements, purchase orders, and other authorized
expenditures, subject to applicable budget and procurement requirements.

Fiscal Analysis:
The proposed change does not result in an increase to TTD’s budget or authorize additional
expenditures.

Work Program Analysis:
Implementation of the proposed increase in signing authority is consistent with TTD’s ongoing work
program and is intended to improve administrative efficiency in carrying out approved activities.

Background:
The Executive Director currently has authority to execute contracts, agreements, purchase orders,
and other related documents on behalf of TTD up to $75,000. Transactions exceeding this amount
require additional Board approval.

As TTD’s programs and operations continue to evolve, staff is requesting an increase in the Executive
Director’s signing authority to $100,000. The proposed increase would provide greater administrative
flexibility and allow routine business matters to be processed more efficiently while maintaining
appropriate financial oversight.

Discussion:
Increasing the Executive Director’s signing authority from $75,000 to $100,000 would streamline the
approval process for expenditures and agreements that are within TTD’s approved budget and
established programs. This change would reduce the need to bring relatively routine transactions to
the Board solely because they exceed the current signing threshold.
